files.purpose: The thread's bottom terminal drawer: TerminalPanel (4-111) draws the 38-point tab row (a horizontally scrolling strip of TerminalTab chips, the plus 'New terminal' chip and the chevron.down 'Hide terminal' chip), then either the selected session's TerminalHost or the 'No shell open in this thread' empty state with a glass 'New shell' button, at the height dragHeight ?? model.settings.terminalHeight, on a top-rounded near-black/near-white sheet, and calls terminals.ensureTerminal on appear. An 8-point overlay strip at the top edge (TerminalResizeHandle, 113-131) resizes the drawer with a 140...760 clamp applied only during the drag and commits to settings on release. The same file keeps the AppKit bridge for the terminal itself: TerminalHost (188-251) re-parents the long-lived SwiftTerm view, re-applies appearance, hands first-responder focus once off the SwiftUI update, and installs a local keyDown monitor that closes the drawer on a bare Escape when the shell owns the foreground; TerminalHostContainer (253-318) parks autoresizing during a window live resize and syncs the terminal frame at most every 50 ms, then once at the end. At B3 the file no longer carries its own AppKit resize strip: TerminalResizeHandle became a SwiftUI View that configures the new shared DragHandle (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift) instead of the B2 NSViewRepresentable plus TerminalResizeHandleView NSView.

SOURCE FACT: B3 TerminalResizeHandle (114-131) is now a SwiftUI View whose body is DragHandle(axis: .vertical, grip: DragHandleView.Grip(restLength: 12, shownLength: 28, thickness: 2.5), cursor: .resizeUpDown, onBegin: onBegin, onChange: { onChange($0.height) }, onEnd: onEnd). Unset DragHandle parameters take their defaults (DragHandle.swift:270-280): dragCursor nil, slop 0, isActive true, onDoubleClick nil; Grip defaults (DragHandle.swift:18-30): alpha 0.6, glowInset nil, refreshesHoverOnLayout false. The TerminalPanel callbacks at 86-96 (onBegin/onChange clamp 140...760/onEnd commit) are unchanged.

SOURCE FACT, unchanged behaviour carried by the shared view (compared line by line against B2 TerminalResizeHandleView at B2 114-256): grip geometry (centred bar 2.5 thick, corner radius thickness/2, 12 rest / 28 shown, opacity 0 / 0.6; DragHandle.swift:159-173), 0.18 s ease-out animation for hover/drag and disabled actions otherwise (DragHandle.swift:58-61, 160-166), labelColor resolved in the effective appearance and repainted on appearance change (DragHandle.swift:91-102), acceptsFirstMouse true and mouseDownCanMoveWindow false (183, 186), cursor rect over bounds (188-192), press records the window location, sets dragging, animates the grip and calls onBegin (198-208 with slop 0), drag reports point.y - pressOrigin.y (210-220, 263), a single tracking area with mouseEnteredAndExited/activeAlways/inVisibleRect (234-245), enter/exit set hover and animate (247-255), layout updates the grip with animations disabled (116-125, refreshesHoverOnLayout false). The added glow layer stays at opacity 0 because glowInset is nil (174-179).

SOURCE FACT, behaviour changed for the terminal strip (inherited from the B2 sidebar handle, B2 WindowChrome.swift SidebarResizeHandleView): (1) mouseUp (DragHandle.swift:222-232) now clears isDragging, calls onChange with the release travel, calls onEnd, and only then re-reads hover from the pointer's actual position (refreshHover, 142-151: window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream converted to the view, bounds.contains) and animates the grip; B2 (B2 TerminalPanel.swift:232-237) called onChange, cleared isDragging, animated the grip from the tracked isHovering flag, then called onEnd. Upstream's comment at DragHandle.swift:229 says no exit arrives while the button is held, so after a drag that ends with the pointer off the strip B3 hides the grip at release where B2 kept it shown from a stale hover flag. The final-delta-before-onEnd order that PR-TERM-015 relies on is preserved. (2) mouseUp now returns early unless a drag is in progress (223). (3) viewDidMoveToWindow (127-138), which B2's terminal strip did not override, now reads the pointer's actual position when the strip enters a window and applies the grip without animation, so a drawer that appears under a resting pointer shows the grip at once; and if the strip leaves its window mid-drag, isDragging is cleared (no cursor pop, dragCursor is nil) and onEnd is not called. (4) isActive and hitTest(_:) (49-56, 194-196) exist but are always active for the terminal strip; clickCount == 2 calls onDoubleClick, which is nil here (200).

Everything from TerminalTab to the end of the file (TerminalTab, TerminalHost, TerminalHostContainer) is textually unchanged; every spec citation into B2 258-443 only needs its line numbers lowered by 125.

Port consequence: the terminal's resize strip and the sidebar edge are one shared control upstream at B3; units.json has no unit for DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift yet, and App.Views.Terminal.TerminalPanel should gain a dependency on it.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: whether, at B2, AppKit would have delivered the missed mouseExited on the first mouse move after the release (which would bound the stale-hover window to 'until the pointer next moves'). Upstream's own comment (DragHandle.swift:229, and B2 WindowChrome.swift SidebarResizeHandleView.mouseUp) only states that no exit arrives while the button is held. The B3 behaviour itself (hover decided from the cursor at release) is a source fact either way.

UNRESOLVED: whether an Avalonia pointer capture released on PointerReleased raises PointerExited for a pointer that left the strip during the drag; the port must not rely on it and should read the pointer position at release instead, as B3 does.

Observation for the DragHandle.swift bundle, not this file: when the strip leaves its window mid-drag (for example the drawer toggled closed while the button is held), B3 clears the handle's drag state without calling onEnd, so TerminalPanel's onEnd never resets runtime.isTerminalResizing; whether that leaves isTerminalResizing true at runtime depends on ThreadRuntime/ChatView code outside this file.
